gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: It was the manager's job to ___ the bad news to the staff.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the news to somebody
gaps.explanation: break the news to somebody means to tell them something difficult or upsetting first.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our shopping at the local market every Saturday.
gaps.explanation: do the shopping is the collocation for buying food and household goods.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.
